items.content_html:
This PR fixes two sets of problems:

  1. Mutable containers did not eval; see #553728 (comment)
  2. The assertions were not accurate
    • Socket availability requires both options on the host
    • Tests the assumption behind the assertion logic by introducing test containers-imperative-no-daemon: Nix is required, but a daemon is not.
    • Report proper assertions, not an error wrapped in a brief but obscure error

(1) tested by building:

nix build -f example.nix --debugger --ignore-try

example.nix

let
  module = { lib, config, ... }: {
    containers.blahaj-bot = {
      autoStart = true;

      bindMounts = {
        "/var/lib/ferretdb" = {
          hostPath = "/data/blahaj-bot/db";
          isReadOnly = false;
        };

        "/etc/blahaj-bot/config" = {
          hostPath = "/run/agenix/blahaj-bot-config";
          isReadOnly = true;
        };
      };

      flake = "https://git.robotcowgirl.farm/transgwender/blahaj-bot/archive/main.tar.gz";
    };
  };
in
with import ./. { }; # living on the edge
(nixos {
  imports = [ module ];
  boot.loader.grub.enable = false;
  fileSystems."/".fsType = "a";
  fileSystems."/".device = "a";
}).toplevel

Darwin does not support nspawn (duh!) so we can't run nspawn tests natively.
But we can run them in a qemu VM... which is what this PR does.

Caveats:

  • no mixed tests (containers + nodes);
  • no interactive mode;
  • obviously, this is slower than running nspawn tests natively.

Interactive mode is doable but I prefer to delay it to after
#543078 lands in some shape.

(h/t @jfly for the idea!)

items.content_html:
Assisted-by: Claude Code (Claude Opus 5)

Adds services.dynacat. I packaged Dynacat in #562771 and this is the follow-up PR with the matching NixOS module.

Since Dynacat is a fork of Glance, this module is heavily based on the existing glance.nix. A new module is needed rather than reusing Glance's because:

  • Some settings differ such as assets-path, cache-dir, db-path and allow-editing which don't exist in Glance.
  • Users may want to run both dashboards.
  • Dynacat resolves its OIDC endpoints at startup and won't start at all if the issuer is unreachable, so the unit orders on network-online.target rather than following Glance network.target.
  • The config schemas match today but may diverge in the future.

It is important to note that Dynacat's default config is to allow-editing set to True but this module changed that to False. The NixOS config is regenerated on every start, meaning editor changes don't survive a restart anyways and if the user has not configured an auth section anyone who can reach the port could rewrite the config. Enabling editing requires an explicit flip to True to acknowledge their edits would be lost after restart. There's precedent on other modules such as home assistant.

Testing

Added a test that covers a defaults-only start, secret substitution, and the editor being off by default and on when enabled. The change to pkgs/by-name/dy/dynacat/package.nix just adds passthru.tests.service so future version bumps run it.

items.content_html:
On Wayland compositors, global input listening requires reading raw /dev/input/* device nodes. Upstream showmethekey handles this by having the GUI frontend (showmethekey-gtk) spawn the backend CLI (showmethekey-cli) via pkexec.

On NixOS, this currently fails out of the box for two reasons:

  1. pkexec lacks setuid root permissions unless security.polkit.enablePkexecWrapper = true is set, producing pkexec must be setuid root.
  2. Users who prefer to avoid enabling a system-wide pkexec SUID binary have no supported way to run showmethekey without manually adding their user to the input group (which exposes a continuous keylogger attack surface across all user processes).

This PR introduces programs.showmethekey to configure proper integration out of the box.
I Added nixos/modules/programs/showmethekey.nix with options:

  • programs.showmethekey.enable: Exposes the package and its Polkit action files system-wide.
  • programs.showmethekey.useSetuidWrapper: (Default: false) Generates a dedicated setuid root wrapper for showmethekey-cli at /run/wrappers/bin/showmethekey-cli and patches showmethekey-gtk to invoke the wrapper directly, removing the dependency on pkexec.

items.content_html:
Description of changes

When the redirect check fails, every remedy the error message offers assumes the
reader is working inside a nixpkgs checkout:

    Added new content?
        $ redirects add-content <identifier> <path>
...
    NOTE: Run the right nix-shell to make this command available.
        Nixpkgs:
        $ nix-shell doc
        NixOS:
        $ nix-shell nixos/doc/manual

NOTE: If your build passes locally and you see this message in CI, you probably
need a rebase.

But the check is also reachable from an ordinary NixOS configuration: any
out-of-tree module setting meta.doc contributes an identifier that
nixos/doc/manual/redirects.json cannot list, so nixos-manual-html fails and
nixos-rebuild stops. This was reported in #412451 and resolved in #412731 by
adding documentation.nixos.checkRedirects.

That option is the right escape hatch, but nothing in the error message points
to it, so a user who hits this has no way to get from the failure to the fix.
This adds one note:

    NOTE: Building a NixOS configuration rather than working on nixpkgs itself?
        An out-of-tree module that sets `meta.doc` contributes identifiers that
        nixos/doc/manual/redirects.json cannot list. Skip this check with the
        NixOS option:

            documentation.nixos.checkRedirects = false;

No behaviour change -- the text of one existing error message only.

Reproducer

mymod.md:

# My Fake Thing {#module-services-myfakething}

mymod.nix:

{ lib, ... }:
{
  options.services.myFakeThing.enable = lib.mkEnableOption "my fake thing";
  meta.doc = ./mymod.md;
}

Adding mymod.nix to a configuration and building
config.system.build.manual.manualHTML fails with
module-services-myfakething. Confirmed on nixos-26.05 (a9e6d84) and
nixos-unstable (2c423e0).

Things done

  • Built on platform(s): x86_64-linux
  • Text-only change to an existing diagnostic; no functional change.
